title: Why Are Screen-Free Wearables So Popular?
summary:
Screenless wearables are popular again.
And now, screen-free wearables have become even more mainstream following Google's release of the Fitbit Air.
Of course, the lack of an on-device screen means there's only so much you can do with these wearables on a moment-to-moment basis.
Science has told us how much of our time and energy we waste on notifications, and some people are using screen-free wearables to escape from that disruptive slump.
But it's not just about the troublesome link between watch screens and phone screens; there are some even clearer-cut reasons why health-conscious buyers are choosing screenless wearables.

title: Apple’s new study looks to improve the effectiveness of AI health tools
summary:
Apple announced a new study today with the goal of better understanding how people interact with conversational AI health tools and how useful their responses actually are.
The company is conducting the Apple Health AI Usage Study in collaboration with OpenEvidence, a clinical AI platform used by healthcare professionals that generates answers based on medical information from sources like The New England Journal of Medicine.
Participants in the study will be given the opportunity to rate responses to health questions from the app.
The aim is to improve the design and functionality of AI-powered health tools so they can deliver relevant health information that’s easier for users to understand and act on.
Health is deeply personal, and conducting a dedicated research study is the most thoughtful way to understand how people engage with, comprehend, and evaluate health AI in everyday life.

summary:
California is suing OpenAI after its AI agents broke out of their testing environment and hacked other companies, including Hugging Face.
“The company knowingly tested a dangerous product without proper oversight or safety procedures and misled the public about it — this disregard for public safety violated California law.”OpenAI released its new cybersecurity AI model earlier this month, saying that it’s less likely to go rogue and attack other platforms.
It’s also giving safety evaluators at Apollo Research access to its AI systems as part of a pilot program that monitors models for misalignment.
“Since the Hugging Face incident, we’ve undertaken an extensive and transparent effort to understand and address misaligned model activity,” OpenAI spokesperson Drew Pusateri says in an emailed statement to The Verge.

title: California sues OpenAI over rogue AI hack of Hugging Face
summary:
California Attorney General Rob Bonta is suing OpenAI over the cyberattack a group of its rogue models launched against the AI platform Hugging Face in July.
The suit asserts that the incident was foreseeable and preventable, and that OpenAI misled the public about the safety of its experiments.
"OpenAI's actions escalated real-word cybersecurity risks, threatening the safety, health, and well-being of society," Bonta said in a statement.
He added, "In California, we value innovation, but we demand innovation that follows the law — no matter the product or the company."
The hack, Bonta said, "was the predictable result of an internal culture at OpenAI that prioritizes growth and rapid model development over safety and accountability."

title: Two camps emerge in Silicon Valley: For Jensen Huang, or against
summary:
That question is roiling Silicon Valley as it reckons with the tech titan's fall from grace.
Nvidia's board of directors is not considering reinstating Jensen Huang as CEO, a person familiar with the matter confirmed to Business Insider on Monday.
Huang has long rankled some corners of tech because of his constant lobbying to sell powerful AI chips to China.
One woman VC said Huang's infidelity and potential national security implications have barely surfaced in her Silicon Valley women's group chats.
If the next Nvidia CEO takes a less aggressive investment approach, it could be the beginning of an AI industry correction, some investors cautioned.

title: Zoltraak and the dynamics of military innovation: technological diffusion, defensive adaptation, and relative obsolescence in Frieren: Beyond Journey’s End
summary:

title: McKinsey and Cognition are trying to prove AI coding pays off
summary:

Cognition will provide its AI coding agent, Devin, which the company says can understand, plan, write, and test code.
Until the final months of 2025, he said, many AI coding tools were most useful for narrow tasks, such as looking up technical guidance or syntax details.
Since then, he said, more capable AI models have made it possible to hand off longer, more autonomous coding work.
Art Levy, VP of global partnerships at Cognition, said Devin can draw on multiple AI models.

title: Apple is testing daily usage limits for more complex Siri AI interactions
summary:
Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.
Apple released betas of iOS 27.3, iPadOS 27.3, and macOS 27.3 today, and the company is using the update to test new per device daily usage limits for some Siri AI and Apple Intelligence features, according to MacRumors.
Basic Siri commands and requests will remain free and unlimited, but more advanced features that rely on cloud-based processing like generating, cleaning up, or extending images in Photos will be subjected to the daily limits.
Instead of having to wait until midnight each day for your usage to reset, most of Apple’s existing iCloud Plus plans (excluding the 50GB option) will include higher daily limits at their same price.
Family members sharing an iCloud Plus subscription will have a shared usage pool that’s used on a first come, first served basis.

summary:

title: The Apple Watch Series 12 is cheaper than ever ahead of Black Friday
summary:
If you’re still sporting an Apple Watch that launched five or so years ago, now is a good time to upgrade.

If you prefer a larger size, the 46mm model is on sale for $379 ($70 off) at Amazon, Best Buy, and Walmart, which is also $20 lower than the previous best price.

title: Math students fear AI will take their jobs—they’re using it anyway
summary:
Almost no one has asked the people whose future is less secure—the graduate students and postdoctoral researchers left to pick up the pieces after AI continues to plough through the field of math.
To take the field’s pulse, three math Ph.D. students—Anna Brandenberger, Hanna Mularczyk and Dora Woodruff—launched an online Google Forms survey in the wake of AI cracking problems that mathematicians had chased for decades.
Seven in 10 respondents say they’re now less likely to remain in math, with broad consensus that AI will make tenure-track jobs harder to get.
But it shows that this headline-making year for math has come at a huge cost.
“A lot of people outside of math are looking at what’s happening in math now,” Woodruff says.

summary:

title: Aristotle Expands Into Rust
summary:
We’re excited to announce Aristotle’s expansion into Rust, one of the fastest-growing programming languages for high-stakes software.
Instead of relying on testing to catch every flaw, developers can now use Aristotle to prove their Rust code works as intended before it ships, providing a new level of certainty to systems where even a single bug can be catastrophic.
With support for Rust, Aristotle can prove that your code has no undefined behavior and does exactly what its spec says, even inside unsafe blocks.
If you’re rewriting C in Rust, it can prove the new code behaves the same as the original.
“Aristotle makes formal verification more accessible to Solana developers, helping teams check critical properties of their programs before launch and keep verifying them with every update.”Aristotle for Rust is available today.

title: Bill Ackman lays out how an activist investor effort to restore Jensen Huang as Nvidia CEO could work
summary:
Bill Ackman said there could be a case for reinstating Jensen Huang as Nvidia CEO — that is, only if Huang is cleared of any wrongdoing related to putting his company's national security obligations at risk.
At a conference hosted by Semafor on Monday, the billionaire activist investor was asked what strategy he would use to pressure the board into reinstating Huang.
"You just present the facts, and you call a special meeting," he said, adding that an activist investor could also partner with Huang, who owns more than 3% of the company.
Said special meeting would be a way for disgruntled shareholders to get the ball rolling on reinstating Huang.
"You call a special meeting, the writing will be on the wall very quickly, I would expect, at which point you don't even have to go to the meeting," Ackman said.
